newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cesp Eurobond put off till April.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cesp Eurobond put off till April.

text.p: Sao Paulo state power company Cesp will launch its 10-year $200 million Eurobond in April, not in March as originally planned, international affairs chief Octavio de Barros said.
"We want to wait until after the Federal Reserve Board's March 25 meeting to see what the market reaction might be to a possible hike in interest rates," Barros said.

He noted that market conditions have worsened since early February, when Cesp chose J.P. Morgan to lead manage the deal. Increasing speculation over a possible hike in short-term U.S. rates has pressured U.S. bond yields this week.

"We are not worried because there is still strong appetite for the bond. This is not a postponement. We just want to see what the best price will be so we don't want to do anything before the Fed meeting," Barros said.
He said there was no way the bond would price in March and that it would almost certainly come in April.
The $200 million bond is the first tranche of Cesp's total $500 million Eurobond program this year. The remaining debt could be issued in one or two tranches, Barros said.
